extraction.name: C-EVAL
extraction.description: A Multi-Level Multi-Discipline Chinese Evaluation Suite for Foundation Models. It comprises multiple-choice questions across four difficulty levels: middle school, high school, college, and professional, spanning 52 diverse disciplines ranging from humanities to science and engineering.
extraction.creator: Yuzhen Huang, Yuzhuo Bai, Zhihao Zhu, Junlei Zhang, Jinghan Zhang, Tangjun Su, Junteng Liu, Chuancheng Lv, Yikai Zhang, Jiayi Lei, Yao Fu, Maosong Sun, Junxian He
extraction.citeAs: Huang, Y., Bai, Y., Zhu, Z., Zhang, J., Zhang, J., Su, T., Liu, J., Lv, C., Zhang, Y., Lei, J., Fu, Y., Sun, M., & He, J. (2023). C-EVAL: A Multi-Level Multi-Discipline Chinese Evaluation Suite for Foundation Models. arXiv:2305.08322v3.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data was collected from mock exams freely available on the internet, past exam questions from top universities in China publicly shared by students, and mock questions for the national graduate entrance exam sourced from the Weipu website. Most samples were sourced from PDF or Microsoft Word documents on the Internet, rather than plain text or structured questions.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Document analysis, Web Scraping, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Mock exams, past exam questions from top universities in China, mock questions for the national graduate entrance exam from the Weipu website. Formats include PDF, Microsoft Word documents, and web pages.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Questions with fewer than four options were eliminated, and incorrect choices were randomly dropped for questions with more than four options to ensure all questions have exactly four choices.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: PDF documents were initially processed into text. Questions were parsed automatically when possible, and otherwise manually by the authors into a structured format. Complex mathematical notations were manually converted into standard LaTeX formats. The data underwent deduplication and cleaning, followed by several rounds of human validation. Questions were randomly split into development, validation, and test sets (1:9 ratio for validation:test).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Authors parsed and carefully annotated data from PDF or Word documents into a structured format. For the development split, GPT-4 was prompted to generate step-by-step explanations for the ground-truth answers, which were then manually revised by the authors to obtain the final explanations.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: A public leaderboard is maintained at https://cevalbenchmark.com. Ground-truth labels for the test split are kept private to ensure fair use; users must submit predictions to obtain test accuracy.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Helps analyze important strengths and shortcomings of foundation models and fosters their development and growth for Chinese users. Addresses the gap in evaluation for Chinese LLMs, moving beyond English-centric benchmarks which exhibit geographical biases towards the domestic knowledge of the regions that produce them.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: There are fluctuations in the proportion of different answer options (A, B, C, D), though they are relatively small around a random 25% level.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark is far from perfect for LLM evaluation; it does not cover abilities such as reasoning over and calling APIs, nor aspects extending beyond accuracy including safety, bias, and robustness. Potential data leakage issues exist (mitigated by using mock/local exams and PDF sources). Many subjects are not reasoning-intensive.
